summary: Four candidate documents directly apply boosted decision-tree ensembles to wildfire mapping as their primary contribution. [V0184] (Fischer et al., 2022) applies boosted decision-tree ensembles to mapping active wildfire extent on the Atlas-ICU dataset, achieving a test F1 of 0.93 — the highest performance among the directly relevant studies. [V0183] (El-Sayed et al., 2021) applies the same method to wildfire extent mapping on the MetroFlow dataset, reporting AUROC 0.86. [V0181] (Chen et al., 2019) revisits wildfire extent mapping with boosted decision-tree ensembles on the FireScope dataset, achieving accuracy 0.72. [V0182] (Duarte et al., 2020) applies boosted decision-tree ensembles to wildfire extent mapping on ChurnBench, reporting MAE 0.79. A fifth slot is filled by [V0087] (Adebayo et al., 2026), which applies boosted decision-tree ensembles but to battery remaining life estimation (AUROC 0.88 on GridWatch), not wildfire mapping — included only because no additional directly relevant wildfire+GBT documents exist among the candidates. All other candidates either use a different method, address a different task, or only mention wildfire mapping as prior work rather than as their own application.

claims.attribute: Best reported F1 for wildfire mapping (Atlas-ICU dataset)
Boosted decision-tree ensembles applied to non-wildfire task (battery remaining life, GridWatch AUROC)
